results.strategy_description: The TabCap Balanced Credit Fund (TBAL) aims to generate returns while maintaining a low correlation to global equity and credit markets. The strategy is systematic in nature and takes both long and short exposure to credit options and credit indices, aiming to exploit inefficiencies in the credit volatility market while remaining market neutral. TBAL uses a systematic approach to monetising inefficiencies in credit option markets offering uncorrelated returns vs. market beta and common factors. TBAL's core instruments are credit default swap indices and credit index options. Certain credit index options are continually overvalued while others are undervalued given the ongoing structural flows and barriers to entry. The core of TBAL is a proprietary systematic strategy that is designed to benefit from these pricing inefficiencies. In addition, the team can actively adjust the core systematic strategy over time to take advantage of changing market opportunities.

results.strategy_description:
The Tabula Liquid Credit Income UCITS Fund (TLIQ) is a long-biased liquid credit strategy that uses CDS index products and seeks to generate a high income with downside protection, while remaining compliant with UCITS rules. TLIQ aims to outperform traditional high yield investments over the long term by taking advantage of the high risk-adjusted return of CDS indices relative to corporate bonds. TLIQ uses leveraged investment grade exposure rather than unlevered high yield exposure to generate returns and has low interest rate exposure. TLIQ’s core instruments are highly liquid credit indices, credit index options and government bond collateral. TLIQ has an embedded systematic tail-risk hedging strategy to mitigate downside risk during large market shocks. The proprietary systematic strategy generates return through three main components:
• An income portfolio, where income is generated through a rolling long risk position in the iTraxx Main and CDX IG indices;
• A hedge portfolio, where a systematic programme of credit payer options is used to protect the Fund from downside risk; and
• A risk-free rate from collateral assets within the fund. 
TabCap’s proprietary analytics actively monitor markets for ways to generate relative outperformance while retaining a similar risk profile. When such instances are identified, the strategy may employ an active fund management overlay which allows an active divergence from the core systematic strategy. Risk controls limit the amount that the portfolio managers can deviate from the core systematic strategy.

results.strategy_description:
Maverick Long Enhanced targets 130% long exposure and 100% short exposure, resulting in approximately 100% net market exposure.  The portfolio is invested primarily in medium- and large-cap equities, diversified by both region and industry.  Performance is driven by individual security selection, rather than market timing, sector rotation, or index trading.

Maverick’s fundamental research process devotes significant resources to every investment decision.  A team of 32 research and trading professionals seeks the best long and short opportunities globally, guided by risk-reward dynamics rather than value or growth style factors, market capitalization or index weighting.  While bottom-up fundamental analysis drives security selection, quantitative research plays a critical role in portfolio construction and risk management.

The investment team is structured into four sector groups—Consumer, Healthcare, Cyclicals, and Technology—supported by two dedicated private investment teams (Silicon and Ventures), as well as specialized quantitative research and trading teams.  Team members are responsible for developing both long and short ideas, deepening analytical expertise and enhancing their understanding of competitive dynamics.  Collectively, the 32 investment and trading professionals average 14 years of industry or investment experience and nine years of tenure at Maverick.

Our investment and operating decisions are guided by the principle of placing investors’ interests ahead of all other considerations.  We strive to maintain the highest standards of integrity and ethical conduct.  Those standards are embodied in our Code of Conduct to which all our partners and employees are personally committed.  Maverick investors enjoy transparency, confidentiality and consistent treatment.  Our overarching objective is to develop and maintain a reputation for both ethical conduct and a record of performance in which every Maverick partner and employee can take great pride.
results.strategy_description:
Maverick’s Hedged Equity Strategy generally targets 120% long exposure and 80% short exposure, resulting in approximately 40% net market exposure.  The portfolio is invested primarily in medium- and large-cap equities, diversified by both region and industry.  Performance is driven by individual security selection, rather than market timing, sector rotation, or index trading.

Maverick’s fundamental research process devotes significant resources to every investment decision.  A team of 32 research and trading professionals seeks the best long and short opportunities globally, guided by risk-reward dynamics rather than value or growth style factors, market capitalization or index weighting.  While bottom-up fundamental analysis drives security selection, quantitative research plays a critical role in portfolio construction and risk management.

The investment team is structured into four sector groups—Consumer, Healthcare, Cyclicals, and Technology—supported by two dedicated private investment teams (Silicon and Ventures), as well as specialized quantitative research and trading teams.  Team members are responsible for developing both long and short ideas, deepening analytical expertise and enhancing their understanding of competitive dynamics.  Collectively, the 32 investment and trading professionals average 14 years of industry or investment experience and nine years of tenure at Maverick.

results.strategy_description:
BlueBalance Global Opportunities is a discretionary RV/Macro strategy that aims to profit from dislocations across term structures in equities, rates, and FX. The strategy has a track record of more than 10 years. The portfolio mainly consists of non-directional, relative value transactions, as well as macro- and volatility trades. The strategy invests across liquid asset classes primarily via derivatives and focuses on medium- to long-term structural dislocations that are considered significantly more interesting and less crowded than at the short end of the curve. To mitigate drawdowns inherent in relative value trades during a correlation shock, the strategy constantly holds a hedging book, which seeks to smooth returns over the long term by softening the left tails. The hedging book primarily engages in capital-efficient long volatility transactions.
The strategy aims to provide the broadest possible diversification with consistent returns, independent of market direction and without major drawdowns. The Fund target a double-digit return, with a Sharpe ratio above 1, indicating a superior risk-adjusted performance.

results.strategy_description:
BlueBalance Global Opportunities is a discretionary RV/Macro strategy that aims to profit from dislocations across term structures in equities, rates, and FX. The strategy has a  track record of more than 10 years. The portfolio mainly consists of non-directional, relative value transactions, as well as macro- and volatility trades. The strategy invests across liquid asset classes primarily via derivatives and focuses on medium- to long-term structural dislocations that are considered significantly more interesting and less crowded than at the short end of the curve. To mitigate drawdowns inherent in relative value trades during a correlation shock, the strategy constantly holds a hedging book, which seeks to smooth returns over the long term by softening the left tails. The hedging book primarily engages in capital-efficient long volatility transactions.
The strategy aims to provide the broadest possible diversification with consistent returns, independent of market direction and without major drawdowns. The UCITS's target return is 4-6% above the risk-free rate, with a Sharpe ratio above 1, indicating a superior risk-adjusted performance.

results.exact_name: Vision Opportunity Master Fund Limited Partnership
results.management_company_description:
Vision Capital Corporation (“Vision”),  registered as a Portfolio Manager, Investment Fund Manager and Exempt Market Dealer with the Ontario Securities Commission and reports to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) as an exempt reporting adviser, is the Manager of the Vision Opportunity Funds (the “Funds”), alternative investment funds that focus on investments in publicly-traded securities in the real estate sector. 

Vision targets inefficiencies that generate a lower cost base, less risk and superior liquidity compared to direct property investments. The Funds have the flexibility to invest globally; however, they operate primarily in North America to benefit from unique inefficiencies inherent in the pricing of select U.S. and Canadian publicly-traded real estate securities.

Vision employs a value-based approach in a long-short equity strategy and selectively utilizes active investing strategies to improve total returns. 

Vision brings to the Funds a collective wealth of knowledge and experience, spanning over 100 years, of its portfolio management team members: Jeffrey Olin, Frank Mayer, and Andrew Moffs, who possess a deep understanding of the real estate sector along with valuable insights and well-established industry relationships.
results.strategy_description:
Vision Opportunity Master Fund Limited Partnership (the "Fund") is the "master fund" in a master-feeder structure, in which Vision Opportunity Fund Limited Partnership, Vision Opportunity Fund Trust, Vision Opportunity U.S. Fund Limited Partnership, and Vision Opportunity TE & Non-U.S. Fund Limited Partnership, operating as "feeder funds", invest all of their subscription proceeds in the Fund to achieve their investment objectives. 

The Fund has a significant real estate focus and invests primarily in North America, including a focus on market inefficiencies unique to Canada and selectively in the United States. Where appropriate, Vision will seek to be an active investor by utilizing the combination of its real estate experience together with its capital market knowledge and relationships to benefit the Fund. The Fund may be selectively concentrated in Vision's best ideas as it seeks to identify specific opportunities to capitalize on the arbitrage between private and public real estate valuations. Portfolio investments in the Fund can be long or short, although Vision has historically had a majority of investments as long holdings reflecting the aforementioned market inefficiencies which will enable the Fund to have exposure to real estate investment more cheaply through the stock market than in the property market.

Vision uses an active management approach to achieve the Fund’s investment objectives of generating consistently favorable risk-adjusted total returns to investors. Vision employs numerous quantitative and qualitative factors to identify and profit from trends and mispriced securities that do not adequately reflect the underlying value and growth prospects of the issuer. 

Vision's investment strategy seeks out undervalued or overvalued corporations/REITs both absolutely and relative to their peers. The strategy involves the identification of corporations’/REITs’ Net Asset Value (NAV) of the underlying real estate as compared to the pricing of its equity (or debt) securities. Focusing on NAV: i) avoids excessive and myopic focus on near-term earnings and cash flow; and, ii) assesses impact from (undervalued or off-balance sheet) assets which do not have current earnings or liabilities which may not be sufficiently understood.

The strategy utilizes a combination of “top-down” and “bottom-up” approaches to pinpoint investment opportunities. A top-down strategy for assessing asset sectors or regions, and a bottom-up approach to select specific investments based on the merits of the specific entity and preference for internalized and aligned management. Vision also assesses balance sheet considerations including near-term liquidity factors. The strategy also involves investments in debt, convertible debt, and preferred shares, particularly when equity-like returns are available with a lower level of risk.

results.management_company_description:
Versor Investments was founded in January 2014 by Founder and Managing Partner Deepak Gurnani and Founding Partners: Ludger Hentschel, Andrew Flynn, DeWayne Louis, and Nirav Shah. Versor is a pioneer in applying AI and alternative data to global equity markets. As a quantitative equities boutique, we focus on systematically delivering uncorrelated alpha across single stocks, equity index futures, and corporate events. Versor’s 50+ professionals drive the creation and implementation of alpha forecast models, risk models, portfolio construction and the trading process.

Asset Under Management data as of June 30, 2025.  AUM based on internal estimates. AUM as per SEC definition for the purposes of Item 5.F on the Form ADV Part 1a.
results.strategy_description:
The Merger Arbitrage strategy invests in announced merger deals across the US, Canada, UK, and Europe and capitalizes on the spread between a company’s current share price and its acquisition price. The strategy uses an active fundamental investment style, based on 20+ years of merger arbitrage investing experience, combined with superior systematic processes and technology. Every step of the investment process relies on solid fundamental and economic theory. Sophisticated machine learning techniques are used to process vast amounts of information saved in a proprietary merger database. 

Alternative data sources track real-time merger data and a proprietary database of 4000+ deals (since 2000) stores both fundamental data (on target and acquirer companies) and market data, including intra-day spreads, for the life of the deal. The comprehensive deal-by-deal evaluation process uses machine learning and the proprietary database to estimate probability of deal success versus failure, determine downside risk and perform competing bid analysis. The investment process also incorporates market assessment of valuation and risk & regulatory approvals. Electronic trading significantly enhances trading efficiencies and reduces costs.

We believe that the Versor Merger Arbitrage strategy has one of the highest ESG impacts of any investment strategy. Historically, the ESG scores for the merger targets in the portfolio have improved by 57% from a year prior to the merger to a year after the merger. For investors who seek to raise the ESG standards of publicly listed companies, Versor Merger Arbitrage is likely to be one of the most impactful investment strategies.

results.strategy_description:
The RV Investment Strategy trades a fixed income liquid rates relative value strategy focused on G-7 and eurozone markets. Lykourgos (Lyko) Tsirakis serves as its chief investment officer (“RV CIO”).  

The RV CIO seeks to generate long-term sustainable returns through a combination of relative value and basis fixed income liquid rates strategies, investing primarily in G-7 and eurozone markets.  The RV CIO seeks to structure a diversified strategy, subject to pre-defined value at risk (“VaR”), concentration, liquidity, stress and stop-loss risk limits. This approach attempts to exploit temporary mispricings in the capital markets caused by market segmentation, differing investor preferences, temporary structural features and unanticipated market events.  

The RV Investment Strategy includes bond/futures basis trading, and sub-strategies include asset swap spreads, bond relative value, yield curve relative value, inflation and macro hedging strategies.

Trades for the RV Investment Strategy are primarily expressed using liquid fixed income instruments, with a focus on G-7 and eurozone government bonds, futures, cleared swaps, and the periodic use of options and other instruments.

Diversification is a key component of the RV Investment Strategy. Capital is allocated dynamically without predefined limits across geographies, product types and sub-strategies based on a continuing evaluation of the market environment and opportunity set.

results.management_company_description: Sone Capital Management (“Sone”) was founded in 2024 by George Panos alongside several senior investment and operations professionals from Echo Street Capital Management (“Echo Street”). George founded Sone after 12 years at Echo Street, where he was most recently a Partner and Portfolio Manager. Sone manages a market-neutral equity long/short strategy and employs a structured and repeatable approach to fundamental investing. The Firm is based in New York City and embraces a culture of curiosity, diligence, and urgency.
results.strategy_description: Sone Capital seeks to generate attractive, uncorrelated returns with low volatility through the pursuit of a market-neutral equity long/short strategy. The strategy uses proprietary in-house fundamental Net Asset Value (NAV) data to systematically construct Relative Value (RV) trades within a curated universe of global developed market equities. The universe is comprised of quality companies with durable earnings streams driving stable, narrowly bounded NAVs. Sone’s investment team is responsible for continuously updating the underwriting of NAVs using a Bayesian process, ensuring the integration of new information in real time. The strategy pursues tight fundamental fit of longs and shorts, allowing for leveraged market-neutral exposure, while emphasizing idiosyncratic mispricing. Sone manages this RV strategy using the proprietary data and code base developed over two decades at Echo Street. Portfolio construction incorporates higher gross exposure and little to no net exposure.

results.management_company_description:
DCM Systematic SA is an independent, quantitative investment manager based in Geneva, Switzerland. The business was founded by two senior quants from BlueCrest and they were joined by a head of business development from Pictet. The team launched the flagship strategy, Diversified Alpha, in February 2016. The firm is built upon the premise of applying scientific methods to identify a wide range of opportunities within liquid financial markets. Research is at the core of the business and the team is continually striving to improve by exploring new quantitative methods, learning from the markets and enhancing processes. The aim is that with this approach the company can successfully navigate different market environments and the variety of challenges they present.

In 2022, two experienced portfolio managers joined to launch a new venture called Solken Convertible Arbitrage. This is a distinct product within DCM Systematic and combines quantitative techniques with discretionary analysis to explore opportunities in the convertible bond markets.
results.strategy_description:
DCM RAIF – Solken Convertible Arbitrage pursues an alternative, relative value strategy generically called convertible arbitrage. It consists in identifying convertible securities that trade at a discount to their fair value or whose valuation is expected to fluctuate, and set up hedges in an effort to neutralise traditional market premia and isolate returns generated by the move in relative value of the components. The Fund follows an innovative strategy by building a systematic extension of the
common discretionary approach.

results.strategy_description:
Orion Commodities Fund ("OCF") employs a discretionary, sector-specialist strategy that solely trades precious and base metals via derivatives and physicals.

The fund seeks to achieve uncorrelated, absolute returns with controlled volatility by primarily employing relative-value, calendar spread, and arbitrage trades while maintaining limited directional exposure to metals. Additionally, OCF receives optionality through its ability to take delivery of metals via warehouse receipts (warrants), allowing it to discern the veracity of fundamental trends not readily apparent in outright market price movements while retaining its liquid profile. Currently, the strategy trades the CME (US), LME (London), and SHFE (Shanghai) exchanges.

Since inception, the strategy has maintained low correlation and beta to traditional markets, including equities, fixed income, and even broad commodities – all while controlling downside risk. 

OCF is the hedge fund division of Orion Resource Partners ("ORP"), an $8bn AUM metals and mining investment firm that accesses the global supply chain through its separate private equity, royalty, venture capital, and trade finance divisions.

Through its relationship with its parent firm, OCF is able to access proprietary research and glean additional insight into the underlying fundamental drivers of metals prices, providing it with an edge in the metals trading space.

results.strategy_description: The Asterion strategy is a short-term systematic multi strategy taking directional positions across Global Markets. The strategy utilizes an ensemble approach to extract alpha from short term predictions. It is designed to generate absolute returns by capitalizing on a variety of market behaviors across global futures markets. The strategy exploits inefficiencies and patterns driven by biases and behavior created by a variety of market participants, ranging from sophisticated institutions to activities driven by retail flows. The strategy is designed to overwhelmingly carry directional exposure. While the program aims to be market neutral over a cycle, it will rarely be market neutral on a particular day and may hold positions against the prevailing market trends. The strategy currently trades liquid Futures across a variety of sectors and geographies but may opt for other asset classes to reflect future opportunities and to exploit liquidity pockets (e.g. ETFs, FX Forwards, look-a-like swaps, etc.). The program is set up to be highly dynamic and can shift exposure from neutral to large positive or negative views in any particular market. Unlike traditional CTAs, that tend to heavily depend on long-term trend-based strategies, the Asterion strategy deploys a multitude of different strategies, currently clustered within three families: Mean Reversion, Behavioral, and Trend Following, with a short average holding period. In expectancy terms, over a longer period, the approach utilized by the Asterion strategy seeks to deliver a higher Sharpe ratio compared to a pure Trend Follower strategy as the different families offer uncorrelated returns streams, thereby creating a more robust investment opportunity.

Our specialized investment teams manage a range of long-term, active strategies spanning alternatives, convertibles, equities, fixed income, and multi-asset solutions, bringing extensive experience to these markets and disciplines. Our multi-disciplinary investment platform and collaborative culture empower investment professionals to enhance client outcomes through shared knowledge and insights.

For over 45 years, we have helped clients around the world achieve their investment goals. With a deep focus on risk and return, we continue to uphold our founder’s commitment to long-term performance, excellence in investment management, and client service.
results.strategy_description:
Overview: 

The Calamos International Growth Concentrated Strategy is an active, high-conviction strategy that invests in a concentrated portfolio of common stocks of growth companies based outside the United States with the objective of outperforming the MSCI ACWI Index ex USA over a full market cycle. The strategy inception is December 1, 2013.
 
Key features: 

The strategy is managed by an experienced team of investment professionals that utilize a time-tested process incorporating top-down and bottom-up, fundamental and quantitative elements. This process aims to research and identify the most attractive growth businesses to invest in from outside the United States, across developed and emerging markets –  including those not in the strategy’s benchmark. These businesses typically operate in areas favorably impacted by secular growth themes and exhibit defensible business models with competitive advantages, durable top- and bottom-line growth, high and/or accelerating returns on invested capital, healthy and flexible balance sheets, and strong management teams.

Approach:

We believe investing in high growth businesses that create and compound intrinsic value over time provides attractive returns for our clients. Many investors and the market overall have a shorter-term focus and time horizon when it comes to analyzing businesses, their growth opportunities, and value creation. This often leads to an underappreciation for the duration and magnitude of economic profit growth for innovative and disruptive businesses. As a result, identifying the best growth businesses and understanding what their future may look like, and having a long-term view on how intrinsic value can be created can be an advantage in capturing opportunities. Our investing principles, time-tested process, and experienced team position us well to identify and invest in these great businesses.
